title: Add Deposit works without a core, and Record Deposit has its own methods
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including BOTH Part sales -> Create & Edit AND Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit.
  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: top menu Customers -> New Customer, enter a Name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and click Save.
  3. A part sale with cores in various states (one charged, one returned). Seed: top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale (pick the customer, Save); in the Add Part dialog add two parts, each with Quantity 1, a Vendor and a Core Charge (e.g. $79.99) — click Save & Add Part after the first, Save & Close after the second. Click Authorize, Order both, Receive both (in the Receive parts dialog type a part number and Cost for each, then Receive Parts). Click Return Core on one core row; leave the other core charged.
custom_steps:
1. On the Finance tab, confirm Add Deposit is available whatever state the cores are in.
  2. Use Record Deposit to capture a deposit taken by one of the shop's own methods (choose a Payment Method, enter an Amount).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Add Deposit is available whatever state the cores on the sale are in - a deposit is never gated on a core.
  • Record Deposit captures a deposit taken by any of the shop's own methods, exactly as on a work order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10269 (Take a deposit on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 8; design canvas boards S8_*; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-R6: “A deposit is never gated on a core; it can be added whatever state the cores on the sale are in”
  • S8-R7: “Record Deposit captures a deposit taken by any of the shop's own methods, exactly as it does on a work order”
